turns.t: Hi. Sorry, I almost didn't make it, the snow was... the lot behind the building was a mess.
Tell me about it. They never plow that lot till noon. Come on in. So, you're here about your cycles and your weight?
Yeah. Well, mostly my periods. They're, um, I don't know how to say it. They're all over the place.
What does all over the place look like? Give me an example.
Like, I'll skip a month. Or two. And then I'll get one that lasts, you know, forever.
How long has this been going on?
About eight months, I think. Before that it was, I mean, not perfect, but...
But more regular?
Right. More regular. Every five weeks or so.
Okay. When was your last period?
Um. About seven weeks ago? I'd have to check my phone. I track it but I forgot to look.
That's fine, bring it next time. When you do get one, is it heavy?
It's heavy at the start, then it kind of trickles on. I don't know if that's, like, normal.
It's common with irregular cycles. What's the weight thing? What's bothering you there?
I just feel like I'm gaining and I can't... it doesn't matter what I try. It's frustrating.
I hear you. A lot of my patients feel the same way. Let's get your numbers first.
Weight today is 82 kilograms.
Oh. It's more than last time. I figured.
Slightly. And your blood pressure is 118 over 74, which is great.
Okay. That's good, right?
That's excellent. Now let me have a quick look. Any spots on your face or jawline that bother you?
Yeah, a few. Mostly along my chin. They come and go with my cycle, or what's left of it.
I see a few small acne spots along your jawline, nothing deep.
Is that connected? To the periods?
It can be. Hormones affect skin, cycles and weight all together. That's why I want to look at the hormone side.
So what kind of tests?
I'd like to order a blood test for your hormone levels. You'd get it done at the lab downstairs.
Do I need to fast for that? I hate fasting.
Yes, from midnight, water only. Early morning is best, and the lab opens at seven.
Okay. Is there anything else?
I'm also going to book a pelvic ultrasound, so we can look at your ovaries and the lining of the uterus.
Is that the one where you need a full bladder?
For the one over your belly, yes. Drink about a liter of water an hour before. The tech will tell you more.
A liter. Right. I always manage to forget that and then they send me away...
Set an alarm on your phone. I'll note it on the order so they don't send you away.
Thanks. And in the meantime, should I be doing anything for the weight? I just...
Small, steady changes beat crash plans. Regular meals, more protein and fiber, and some movement you actually enjoy.
I've tried all that. Well, some of that. Not very consistently.
That's honest, and totally normal. Pick one thing and keep it going for a month, rather than ten things for a week.
One thing. Okay. I can probably do that.
The results will help us explain a lot of this. Our front desk will call you when the ultrasound is booked.
Okay. Thank you. I feel like I needed to hear it's not just me.
It isn't. Take care of yourself, and watch the ice out there.

chief_complaint.value: my periods. They're, um, I don't know how to say it. They're all over the place

physical_examination.finding: a few small acne spots along your jawline

clinical_actions.description: Order blood test for hormone levels
Make small, steady lifestyle changes: regular meals, more protein and fibre, enjoyable movement
